newsitem.title: LATVIA: PARLIAMENT PASSES CENTRAL BANK LAW AMENDMENTS.
newsitem.headline: PARLIAMENT PASSES CENTRAL BANK LAW AMENDMENTS.

text.p: Parliament on Wednesday approved amendments to the law on the central bank, which allows members of parliament to nominate the central bank president and vote for him or her, politicians said.
Current central bank chief Einar Repshe was named by the former chairman of the old post-Soviet supreme council, later replaced by a parliament.
The amendments say no less than 10 MPs may nominate a central bank chief, who comes up for reelection in August or September, before a vote in parliament.
Another amendment allows the central bank president to name his own board and deputy president, currently Ilmar Rimshevics.
